summary.text: Amex is the only network whose public rules define a launch gate for issuers. A Beta Test of up to 60 days, a sample card check and a written go-ahead come first.
Amex also commits to review windows at launch. Final advertising gets an answer in 7 to 10 business days and co-brand partners in 10 business days.
Visa and Mastercard rules never use the word pilot. Their go-live is a string of approvals and table loads with no single moment that says a partner is live.
Mastercard's clearest live signal sits in product onboarding. Mastercard Send ends MTF testing with a TAN letter and asks partners to find their first transactions in reconciliation reports.
Card design approval is gated everywhere. Visa wants every design before production, Mastercard routes proofs from the manufacturer through CDAS, and both keep the standards behind a login.
Going live for acquirers means loading the network's range tables fast. Visa gives 6 business days and Mastercard 6 calendar days, and Discover needs an NDA for its full table.
Marks carry published deadlines after launch. PULSE gives issuers 9 and 24 months and ATMs 45 days, Mastercard gives debit issuers 9 and 36 months, and Visa gives ATMs 30 days.
Capital One's move of about 25 million debit cards from Mastercard to Discover is the one large conversion with public detail. It began with pilot populations in June 2025.

The conversion's friction landed on cardholders and merchants. New numbers, a 130-day overlap, instant-transfer gaps, travel acceptance warnings and higher debit interchange all appear in public notices.
Costco's single-day cutover from Amex to Visa in 2016 produced 1.5 million service calls. Walmart's phased 2014 move let old cards work until new ones were active.
Discover's strongest public launch pattern is human. Discover Debit names an implementation project manager for launch, and its API go-live ends in launch support and monitoring.
Early transaction monitoring after launch is thin in public. Visa's rule for day-31 new-merchant exception reports carries an end date of 17 April 2026.

how_it_works.text: The issuer submits every card design, physical or digital, for Visa's written approval before production and again after any change.
In Europe the issuer self-certifies each design on a Card Design Member Self-Certification Form.
Visa's training describes a four-step approval run through the Brand Management Approval System, which card vendors reach on Visa Online.
Restricted-use programmes need an approved Program Information Form and a unique account range before launch.
Within 10 business days of a BIN going live, the issuer must load its contacts into the Client Directory on Visa Access.
The issuer hands Visa its card art for wallets and token requestors, or Visa shows default art.
Regional implementation analysts project-manage new product launches and the twice-yearly release cycle.
Visa's 10-K says client incentive estimates rest on forecasts of card issuance and card conversion.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Access (formerly Visa Online)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Gated client portal that hosts the Client Directory, BMAS and other launch tools, entered with a Business ID.

tools_and_screens.name: Client Portfolio Management Self-Service Tools
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Program Request Management, the electronic Client Information Questionnaire and the Visa Client Support Application, used to manage profile and programme data.

tools_and_screens.name: Brand Management Approval System (BMAS)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Card design submission and approval cases. Screens were not seen because the public copy of the user guide sits behind a CAPTCHA.

friction.text: The rules name no pilot phase and no notice that a programme is live, so the issuer's own directory update is the nearest confirmation.
Visa says its design approval gives no legal protection, so issuers still run their own legal review in parallel.

how_it_works.text: Card rules live in the Card Design Standards, which sit on Mastercard Connect and are incorporated into the rules.
Each co-brand, prepaid or virtual product was registered on a Special Issuer Registration Form in that guide. Prepaid now uses a registration tool on Mastercard Connect.
Mastercard asks issuers to put new programmes on unused account ranges of existing BINs before requesting new ones.
A new debit issuer has nine months to start issuing compliant cards and 36 months to bring the whole portfolio into line.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercard Connect
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Gated portal holding Card Design Standards, My Company Manager and registration applications.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercard Brand Center
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public logo artwork, branding requirements and decal ordering, which sends issuers to Connect for card artwork.

friction.text: The rules contain no pilot or soft-launch concept.

how_it_works.text: Before launch Amex explains the specifications, certifies the issuer, assigns settlement parameters and number ranges and works with its marketing agency.
Issuers certify host messaging and each payment product with Amex teams, test simulators and custom test plans.
Amex and the issuer run a Beta Test of up to 60 days before any sales for each card type or design change.
After the Beta Test and a sample card check, Amex tells the issuer in writing that it may start selling.
The issuer should launch within 45 days of the Beta Test ending.
Mass-media launch campaigns go to Amex 30 days ahead, and the final review comes back in 7 to 10 business days.
Co-brand partners go to Amex at least 60 business days before launch, with an answer in 10 business days.
From launch the issuer files monthly Program Progress Reports within 15 days of month-end.

tools_and_screens.name: Knowledge Base
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Gated library of Network Specifications, card design guidelines and the Issuer Personalization Certification Guide.

tools_and_screens.name: FraudNet, Network Disputes Manager, Program Progress Report
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Operational systems a partner's staff can open only after finishing training.

tools_and_screens.name: Partner Learning
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Webinars and six modules covering over fifty network policies.

friction.text: Amex-led personalisation certification costs 15,000 dollars per certification, charged to the issuer.
Every design change reopens the Beta Test, which slows card refreshes.

how_it_works.text: Capital One is the one large issuer launched onto the network in public view, and it is the network's owner.
Discover publishes no application steps, timelines or fees for new issuing partners.
Capital One lists limited third-party card issuance on its networks as a risk.
For Diners Club issuers, Discover promises extensive implementation support and turnkey marketing programmes.

tools_and_screens.name: Discover Service Center login
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: One MFA login for fraud tools and client portals, with EASI and dispute portals listed alongside.

friction.text: No public document shows how Discover approves card designs for Discover or Diners Club issuers.

best_pattern.text: Amex's written sequence of certification, a capped Beta Test, a sample card check and a go-ahead notice gives both sides one shared definition of launched.

discover_today.text: Discover shows no public issuer launch path beyond its owner's conversion. Third-party issuance is a stated risk and application steps are unpublished.

by_partner.partner_type: Issuers: community banks and credit unions

how_it_works.text: Associate clients hold their own licence and BIN but depend on a principal sponsor for settlement and reporting.
Visa's community-issuer page sends banks and credit unions to a product enrolment portal on Visa Online.
In practice the brand flip follows the processor. Liberty Bay moved to Visa because a new debit processor allowed it.
Clearwater Credit Union reissued every debit card over six months and used Visa Account Updater for saved card details.
Visa Account Updater enrolment is mandatory for most issuer BINs.

tools_and_screens.name: Product enrollment portal (secure.visaonline.com)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Enrolment for Visa products, reached after logging in to Visa Online.

friction.text: Every card changes number, expiry, code and often PIN, and saved payments must be updated by hand where Account Updater does not reach.

how_it_works.text: A US affiliate can join through a Type I processor's ICAs and BINs, so the processor carries most launch work.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercard Connect Store and Prepaid Program Registration tool
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Where products are ordered and prepaid programmes are registered.

friction.text: A debit issuer must bring its whole portfolio into line with card standards within 36 months of first access.

how_it_works.text: Discover Debit names a launch team: a marketing consultant, an account manager and an implementation project manager who sets processes and trains staff.
Every Discover Debit issuer gets the Marketing Hub for banners, social posts, emails and card art.
PULSE issuers must issue compliant new cards within nine months of the first transaction and be fully compliant within 24 months.
Old PULSE marks may stay on cards until they expire or are reissued.

tools_and_screens.name: PULSE Client Support page
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public mark files, the Graphic Standards Manual and separate issuer, processor and acquirer contacts.

tools_and_screens.name: Marketing Hub (debitmarketinghub.com)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Customisable campaigns, card art and cardholder education for Discover Debit issuers.

friction.text: The PULSE Operating Rules are not public, so only the rule excerpts quoted in the graphic manual can be read.

how_it_works.text: NYCE markets joining through the existing EFT processor with no card reissue.

best_pattern.text: Discover Debit's named implementation project manager for launch is the clearest public promise of a person who carries a small issuer to go-live.

discover_today.text: Discover Debit and PULSE already publish a named launch team, a Marketing Hub with card art and public mark rules with deadlines.

how_it_works.text: An acquirer that routes by Visa's Account Range table must install each new table within 6 business days.
A member files a regional client information questionnaire before using a VisaNet processor.
Chip acquirers report terminal test results through the Chip Compliance Reporting Tool on Visa Online.
Tap to Phone solutions and Visa Direct programmes each need Visa approval before launch.
Visa does not accept vendor self-testing for terminal approval and uses accredited labs.

tools_and_screens.name: Chip Compliance Reporting Tool (CCRT)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Submission and management of ADVT test results for deployed chip terminals.

tools_and_screens.name: Approval Services Portal
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Chip product testing and approval, one of four sign-in portals on Visa Digital Partner Services.

friction.text: Visa's new-merchant exception monitoring rule from day 31 carries an end date of 17 April 2026, leaving no prescriptive early-life check in the public rules.

how_it_works.text: Acquirers and anyone holding BIN files for them must apply each Mastercard update within 6 calendar days.
The Member Parameter Extract arrives by Global File Transfer with daily add, change and delete updates.
Host validation ends in a TAN letter, and enrolled acquirers can self-approve terminals or reuse another acquirer's approval.
In the EEA and UK, routing tables must be filed at least five business days before going live.

tools_and_screens.name: Member Parameter Extract (MPE)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Daily BIN and account range table updates for issuers, acquirers and processors.

tools_and_screens.name: Testing Acknowledgement Notification (TAN) letter
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Record of a completed validation session, used as the go-ahead for production.

friction.text: Stale tables cause wrong routing and declines, and Mastercard puts the fix on the acquirer.

how_it_works.text: Acquirers must finish Amex certification before merchant acquiring, covering host and POS terminals.
To certify a POS device, the acquirer sends a request form, interaction logs and receipts to its relationship manager and runs the cases it receives.
Each capability path on the certification page ends with the product being AMEX Enabled.

tools_and_screens.name: Knowledge Base
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Network Specifications and implementation guides needed for host certification.

friction.text: Test cases arrive from a relationship manager, so the path depends on one named contact.

how_it_works.text: Acquirers register for the EASI portal to get specifications, test card kits and a Message Center to operations.
The EASI form asks the company type and the NDA signatory, then emails login credentials.
The public BIN file shows only start, end and length. The full table with product detail sits in EASI under NDA.
Accepting alliance cards and Discover Debit depends on the acquirer loading every Discover range.
Discover's terminal letter of certification lists completed cases, tested interfaces and excluded cases, and accredited acquirers have self-certified since 2013.

tools_and_screens.name: EASI Portal registration
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Form fields for contact, company, company type from acquirer to payment facilitator, regions, business purpose and NDA signatory, with an image verification step.

tools_and_screens.name: Discover host test simulator
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Lets acquirers test at any time and see results immediately.

friction.text: Discover reviews host results within service levels agreed privately, so no public commitment exists.

best_pattern.text: Mastercard pairs a firm table-update deadline with a named TAN letter and lets proven acquirers self-approve terminals.

discover_today.text: Discover offers EASI, a live test simulator and self-certification, but range data needs an NDA and review service levels are private.

how_it_works.text: OptBlue sales agents get a public site with a Merchant Activation Guide, welcome kit and bulk signage ordering.
The activation guide tells agents to get new merchants to post Amex signage on door, register and website.
Merchant Service Providers order signage in bulk on Marketing Corner.
A processor tells Amex Direct merchants to expect processing 2 to 3 business days after sending their merchant ID.

tools_and_screens.name: OptBlue Sales Agent site
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public PDFs for activation, objections, disputes and welcome kits, plus programme updates.

tools_and_screens.name: Marketing Corner
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Bulk point-of-purchase signage orders for providers serving many merchants.

friction.text: Under OptBlue the acquirer, not Amex, services the merchant, so Amex sees launch only through the partner.

how_it_works.text: A payfac must register high-risk sponsored merchants on Mastercard Connect before they accept transactions.
Payfacs must monitor every sponsored merchant on an ongoing basis.
Network Enablement Partner tiers include an Acceptance-Lite package for small payfacs with test ICAs and BINs.

tools_and_screens.name: Specialty Merchant Registration (My Company Performance)
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Pre-launch registration of high-risk sponsored merchants.

how_it_works.text: Visa's acquirer monitoring flags whole portfolios at 50 and 70 basis points of fraud and disputes.

friction.text: Per-item fees began when VAMP enforcement started in October 2025.

how_it_works.text: Payfacs and ISOs register for EASI under their own company type.
An acquirer training video tells sales reps to send merchants to the Discover signage site.

tools_and_screens.name: Discover Signage Site
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Complimentary signage orders behind a login or registration.

friction.text: The public site offers merchants four resources and no agent hub like Amex's.

best_pattern.text: Amex's OptBlue agent site gives the sales channel a public launch kit with activation guide, welcome kit and bulk signage in one place.

discover_today.text: Discover reaches payfacs and ISOs through EASI and a login-gated signage site. No public activation kit for sales agents was found.

how_it_works.text: ATM acquirers install the Visa Account Range table within 6 business days and the Plus table within 3.
Visa and Plus marks must be on every ATM within 30 days of starting to accept the cards.
Issuers pass Visa certification before their cards work in the Global ATM Network.
Independent deployers join as ISO-ATM agents registered by a Visa or Plus client.
Mastercard, Maestro and Cirrus marks must appear on every ATM that accepts them.
PULSE acquirers must put PULSE signage on or near each terminal within 45 days of it going live.
PULSE pitches ATM acquirers exclusive Discover and Diners Club cards and a MoneyPass surcharge-free option.

tools_and_screens.name: PULSE Graphic Standards Manual
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public ATM and POS signage rules, quoting PULSE Operating Rules 4.13 and 8.1.7.

how_it_works.text: A bank guide for new ATM operators puts network access in the processor's hands.

friction.text: Inference: an independent operator reaches networks only through its processor and sponsor, so the network sees little of its launch.

best_pattern.text: Visa and PULSE state go-live deadlines for ATM marks and tables in public rules, which lets operators plan their first 30 to 45 days.

discover_today.text: PULSE publishes ATM signage rules and a 45-day deadline but no public participation steps for ATM acquirers.

how_it_works.text: Non-bank and crypto issuers file a Core Product Program Information Form and need Visa's written approval before issuing.
Fintech Fast Track screens entrants on funding and card experience.
Visa Ready certified partners are offered an integration manager and pilot testing frameworks.
Visa Agentic Ready tests agent transactions in controlled production before wider release.

tools_and_screens.name: Visa Partner
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Programme applications including the Core Product PIF.

friction.text: Platform guides quote 1 to 3 weeks for design approval and 8 to 10 weeks of card production.
Platforms add the sponsor bank's approval of all card art and a proof sign-off as launch steps.

how_it_works.text: Product Express is a digital onboarding platform with pre-certified partners, sold through BIN sponsorship.
Since May 2025 a principal needs Mastercard approval before acting as BIN sponsor for a programme manager.
Processors carry each network release for their fintech clients.

tools_and_screens.name: Product Express portal
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Packaged plans and pre-certified partners for launch.

friction.text: A launch press release naming the network needs the network's pre-approval.

how_it_works.text: Amex fintech cards launch through programme managers and partner banks, as with Hypercard and Coinbase.
Discover assembles BIN sponsors, processors and programme managers and publishes no steps or timeline.
Diners Club launches such as flykk and Nium are announced on Club Connections.

friction.text: One issuing platform's card design docs cover only Visa and Mastercard.
The flykk release is datelined 14 January 2025, so the listing's relative dates mislead readers about recency.

best_pattern.text: Visa Ready offers certified partners pilot testing frameworks and an integration manager, a named bridge from build to launch.

discover_today.text: Discover's fintech route runs through sponsors with no published launch steps, and platform card-design docs often omit Discover.

how_it_works.text: Certification and production credentials need a signed contract and a separate CSR for each environment.
The Onboarding Dashboard collects entity, project, environment and credential details.
Visa says some projects reach production in two weeks and others take months.
Certificate expiry emails go out only for certification and production projects.

tools_and_screens.name: Onboarding Dashboard
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: In-project steps for entity, contact, project, environment request, API registration, users and credentials.

how_it_works.text: Production credentials are issued at once but stay inactive until Mastercard approves.
Mastercom publishes onboarding service levels, including production key approval in 3 business days.
Send assigns a Delivery Manager and a CIS Implementation Manager, and ends MTF with a TAN letter.
Partners confirm go-live by finding production transactions in reconciliation reports and the Customer Portal.

tools_and_screens.name: API status page
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Per-service health for Sandbox and Production, refreshed about once a minute.

tools_and_screens.name: Send Customer Portal
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Where partners check their first production transactions.

friction.text: The Delivery Manager monitors the project, so escalation depends on one person.

how_it_works.text: Going Live with Discover runs certification boarding, API development, certification, production boarding and end-to-end testing.
The last step is Provisioning and Launch, where Discover provides support and monitoring.
Test cases come from Discover during certification boarding.

tools_and_screens.name: Partner Product Portal: Going Live with Discover
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Phase table with client and Discover roles, and a sample timeline without durations.

friction.text: Developer accounts are by invitation from a Discover representative.

best_pattern.text: Mastercard Send tells partners how to prove they are live, by checking first transactions in reports and the portal.

discover_today.text: Discover's go-live table already names a launch phase with Discover support and monitoring, but access is by invitation.

how_it_works.text: Merchants must show Visa marks at every point of sale, including websites and apps.
Signage follows standards posted on the Brand Center, where decals are ordered.

tools_and_screens.name: Mastercard Brand Center
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Public artwork, branding requirements and an Order Decals route.

how_it_works.text: Network acquirers must make every merchant show at least one Amex decal on parity with other networks.
OptBlue merchants are pointed to free Amex signage.
Discover offers free in-store signage and downloadable acceptance marks.
Ordering happens on a separate signage site that needs a login or registration.
Converted Capital One cardholders are told to look for Discover, PULSE or Diners Club logos.

tools_and_screens.name: discoversignage.com
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Login and registration, then complimentary signage ordering.

best_pattern.text: Amex and Mastercard pair a mark rule with a free ordering route that the acquirer channel can use in bulk.

discover_today.text: Discover offers free signage and marks, and asks merchants to register on a separate site to order.

by_partner.partner_type: Converting issuers (portfolio conversions and reissues between networks)

how_it_works.text: Capital One told regulators it would move all debit and a meaningful share of credit to its networks by 2027.
Reissue began with pilot populations in June 2025 and ran in phases into early 2026.
Cards went out account by account. Account number and PIN stayed the same, while card number, code and expiry changed.
Activating the new card turned off the old one, and old cards kept working for 130 days if not activated.
By February 2026 the reissue was substantially complete, and trade press counted about 25 million cards.
Stripe told merchants the debit migration would finish in 2026.
Credit is next. Capital One is testing conversions and planned waves in July, October and January.

tools_and_screens.name: Capital One 'My debit card' page
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Cardholder view of the switch: new card, activation, recurring payments, network changes and FAQs.

tools_and_screens.name: Stripe service notice
tools_and_screens.what_it_shows: Merchant view: account updater fees, higher interchange, 130-day overlap and country coverage.

friction.text: Mastercard network benefits ended on activation, and some payroll and earned-wage providers dropped instant transfers.
Travellers were told to plan for acceptance and cash abroad, and Stripe warned of declines outside Discover coverage.
Merchants saw new Discover BINs with Discover as issuer and uncapped debit rates they cannot avoid.
Venture X and several co-brands stayed on Visa, so one bank now runs two networks for its customers.

how_it_works.text: Costco's Amex cards stopped for new purchases on one day in June 2016 when Citi's Visa cards replaced them.
Credit union flips to Visa follow processor changes and use Visa Account Updater.
Visa prices conversion into client incentives.

friction.text: Citi logged over 1.5 million calls about cards not arriving, activation and online access.
DOJ alleges reissue cost keeps issuers from switching. This is an allegation.

how_it_works.text: Walmart's 2014 move from Discover to Mastercard ran in phases, with old cards working until new ones were active.

friction.text: A new debit portfolio has 36 months to meet card standards, which sets the pace of a reissue.

how_it_works.text: Processors sell migration as a service covering regulation, network engagement, inventory and cardholder communication.
Token vendors pitch keeping stored credentials alive when network identifiers change.

friction.text: Reissuing a whole BIN range at once breaks stored credentials.

best_pattern.text: A phased reissue with pilot groups and an overlap window, as Walmart and Capital One ran, avoids the one-day cutover that swamped Citi.

discover_today.text: Discover has just absorbed the largest recent debit conversion. Its public record shows cardholder and merchant notices but no network-side conversion kit for other issuers.

design_moves.title: A written go-ahead that says you are live
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Make go-live a single network-issued notice. It lists what was certified, the sample card or test result approved, the effective date and the first live transactions seen.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa and Mastercard rules define no pilot and no live moment. Amex's go-ahead notice and Mastercard's TAN letter show partners value a formal artefact.

design_moves.title: A shared first-weeks launch room
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Open a launch view for the first weeks after go-live. It shows approval rates, declines by reason, disputes and the named implementation lead, then hands over to account management.
design_moves.why_advantage: Discover already promises launch monitoring and a named implementation manager. Visa's prescriptive new-merchant checks are ending, so a shared early view fills a gap.

design_moves.title: A conversion kit built from the Capital One reissue
partner_types: Converting issuers (portfolio conversions and reissues between networks)
Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Package conversion as a product. Plan pilot waves, set the overlap window, push account updater, warn merchants and payroll providers, and show acceptance where cardholders travel.
design_moves.why_advantage: Discover is the only network that has just run a large public conversion. The known pain points map to steps a kit can pre-empt.

design_moves.title: Card art once, used everywhere
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Take one card art submission that drives design approval, wallet and token art and Marketing Hub collateral, with status visible to the issuer, processor and card vendor.
design_moves.why_advantage: Visa and Mastercard route design approval through vendors and gated systems. Token art is a separate duty and wallet updates take days to spread.

design_moves.title: Range readiness before cards ship
partner_types: Converting issuers (portfolio conversions and reissues between networks)
design_moves.move: Publish new BIN ranges with effective dates and show issuers which major acquirers have loaded them before cards go out.
design_moves.why_advantage: Every network sets a table-load deadline. No public source shows a network telling issuers whether acceptance is ready, and Discover's full table needs an NDA.

design_moves.title: Marks and deadlines inside the launch checklist
partner_types: Issuers: community banks and credit unions
design_moves.move: Put mark rules, downloads, signage ordering and the post-launch deadlines into the partner's launch checklist, with bulk ordering for acquirers and agents.
design_moves.why_advantage: PULSE already publishes its manual and deadlines openly. Amex gives agents bulk signage, while Discover's signage site needs a separate login.

design_moves.title: Show committed review service levels
design_moves.move: Where the network commits to a review time, show it on the task, for example card art, marketing or co-brand review. Leave estimates out.
design_moves.why_advantage: Amex writes review windows into its policies and Mastercom publishes key approval times. Discover's host review service levels exist but are private.

unseen.what: Visa BMAS screens for card design submission and approval
unseen.why: The only public user guide copy found sits on Slideshare behind a CAPTCHA, which this study does not bypass.
unseen.how_to_see_it: Ask a card vendor or issuer partner for a screen walk, or find a card bureau's published BMAS guide.

unseen.what: Mastercard Card Design Standards and current CDAS workflow
unseen.why: Both sit on Mastercard Connect, and the only public description is a 2011 guide.
unseen.how_to_see_it: Review an issuer or card bureau's copy under NDA, or a recent Mastercard issuer welcome kit.

unseen.what: How Discover and Diners Club approve issuer card designs
unseen.why: No public document describes it. Only card vendor compliance rules are public.
unseen.how_to_see_it: Ask the Discover issuing team for the internal card design approval steps and turnaround.

unseen.what: Network-side early monitoring of newly launched issuers and acquirers
unseen.why: No network publishes a first-weeks monitoring view, and Visa's new-merchant rules are sunsetting.
unseen.how_to_see_it: Interview implementation and account managers at processors about what they watch after go-live.

unseen.what: Merchant and acquirer communications Discover sent during the Capital One debit move
unseen.why: Only processor and consultancy notices are public, not Discover's own bulletins.
unseen.how_to_see_it: Look for acquirer bulletins in the EASI Message Center or ask acquirer partners.

unseen.why: No public Visa signage order site was located, and the web search budget ran out before a wider search.
unseen.how_to_see_it: Search Visa merchant resources pages or ask an acquirer how its merchants get Visa decals.

unseen.what: ATM operator go-live with each network
unseen.why: Independent operators launch through processors and sponsors, and networks publish no operator path.
unseen.how_to_see_it: Interview an ATM processor about network set-up steps, terminal IDs and signage deadlines.

unseen.why: Only the rule excerpts quoted in the Graphic Standards Manual are public.
unseen.how_to_see_it: Request the rules from PULSE or read them through a participating issuer.

unseen.why: Customer Implementation Services and Delivery Manager tools are gated.
unseen.how_to_see_it: Look for processor or bank training material that shows implementation status screens.
